einstellungen.text: Imagine you just won thirty million. And nobody can ever know.
All six numbers. Plus the bonus ball.
Right now, your bank account says eleven dollars and forty cents.
Until a minute ago, that was your biggest problem.
Yesterday you turned eighteen. Grandpa slid an envelope across the table.
“You're old enough now. Good luck, kiddo.”
A lottery ticket. With the same numbers Grandpa has played for forty-one years.
Honestly, you only took it to be polite.
The odds of winning this jackpot are about one in a hundred and forty million.
That's like pointing at one random person in the whole country. Twice in a row.
Every week, millions of people pick their numbers. This time, it's you.
The machine at the kiosk beeps three times. Then for a really long time.
“Kid. You need to go to the lottery office.”
“And tell your grandpa I said hi.”
You run home. The ticket sticks to your sweaty hand.
Thirty million. You could skip school tomorrow. You could never have to do anything again.
You could pay off Mom's house. No more night shifts for Dad. Every pony in the world for Lina.
But something's bugging you.
You flip the ticket over.
On the back, in Grandpa's shaky handwriting: “For all of us.”
